meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Vanuatu (unitary national jurisdiction; corporate registry and financial services regulator: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission, Port Vila)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: English common law as the foundation for company and commercial statutes, French civil law elements, and customary law recognized under Article 95(3) of the Constitution of the Republic of Vanuatu 1980
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER) Plus (in force 2020)
Melanesian Spearhead Group (MSG) Trade Agreement (in force 1993, as amended)
Samoa Agreement (successor to the Cotonou Agreement) between Vanuatu and the European Union

No comprehensive bilateral double taxation agreement network in force; no active bilateral investment treaty with major capital-exporting states; the former limited Australia-Vanuatu double-taxation arrangement has been terminated

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act No. 23 of 2021 (as amended); Vanuatu Financial Services Commission Act No. 10 of 2017; International Companies Act [Cap. 222] (as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Acts 2019-2021, incl. ss. 145A-145H on beneficial ownership registers); Financial Dealers Act [Cap. 191] (Financial Intelligence Unit); Financial Transactions Reporting Act [Cap. 276]; VFSC AML/CFT Rulebook and AML/CFT Guidance Notes for Registered Agents; FATF Recommendations implemented through Vanuatu's membership in the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG)
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access: the beneficial ownership register is maintained by a VFSC-licensed registered agent at the Vanuatu registered office; access is limited to the VFSC, the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit, law-enforcement authorities, and foreign competent authorities via mutual legal assistance; the register is not open to public inspection

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport or immigration authority of the country of issue
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if the issuing country is not party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate (certificate of good conduct) of each beneficial owner and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or criminal-records authority of the applicant's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional bank reference letter (financial probity) covering each beneficial owner and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-jurisdiction bank or financial institution of the account holder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization; letter must be dated within 90 days

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each beneficial owner and director (utility bill or bank statement issued within the last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or financial institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the VFSC-licensed registered agent and, where applicable, a corporate-services provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the grantor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; notarization of signature and grantor identification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Curriculum vitae and professional reference letters of proposed directors (supporting integrity and competence assessment)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization recommended; apostille not strictly required for private CV documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, FATF public statements and increased-monitoring jurisdictions, OFAC SDN List, UK HMT Consolidated Sanctions List, EU autonomous sanctions, and Vanuatu FIU domestic watchlists before onboarding and at least every 180 days thereafter. The AML/CFT Act No. 23 of 2021 defines PEPs to cover foreign, domestic, and international-organization PEPs; any PEP match triggers enhanced due diligence, independent source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, senior-management approval of the registered agent, and retention of enhanced CDD records for a minimum of 5 years after the business relationship ends. Although the stated ISIC 3240 e-commerce line is classified as Low_Risk_Standard, Vanuatu law does not permit exemption from full CDD for International Companies; simplified measures are unavailable where the company is constituted under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222].

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) Company Registry, Port Vila, Republic of Vanuatu - official interface www.vfsc.vu; name clearance is applied for through a VFSC-licensed registered agent using the VFSC name-availability search and the prescribed application form (Form IC-1 with annexure for name reservation), submitted to the Registrar of International Companies
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Roman/Latin script; Bislama, English, French, and any language using the Latin alphabet are acceptable, but the name must be legible, searchable, and recordable in the English-language registry; ideographic or non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic) must be transliterated into Latin characters on the memorandum; the name must not be identical or nearly identical to a name already registered or reserved, and must not be misleading as to the company's nature, activities, or any connection with the Government of Vanuatu. The name of an International Company may carry the suffix 'International Company', 'IC', or 'I.C.', although the Act does not impose a mandatory suffix; the written consent of the VFSC Registrar is required for any deviation from the prescribed naming standards.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection (including a nearly identical or prohibited-name determination), the VFSC Registrar issues a written notice stating the statutory grounds; the applicant, through its licensed registered agent, may file a written request for reconsideration within 14 days of the notice, accompanied by explanatory submissions and any supporting consents or ministerial approvals. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may: (i) file an administrative appeal to the Minister responsible for financial services under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222]; (ii) alternatively or concurrently, make a fresh reservation application with an amended name, refundable only where the Registrar has made a manifest error; and (iii) within 30 days of the final administrative refusal, commence judicial review proceedings in the Supreme Court of Vanuatu. A new name-reservation fee applies to each resubmission.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible. Every International Company must at all times maintain a registered office in Vanuatu and a VFSC-licensed registered agent whose physical address constitutes the registered office (International Companies Act [Cap. 222], ss. 11-12); no local lease, staff, warehousing, or physical plant is required for the stated ISIC 3240 e-commerce activity, which will be sourced and performed outside Vanuatu. To preserve the statutory tax exemption under the International Companies (Exemption) Regulations 2010, the company must not carry on business in Vanuatu, must not own Vanuatu land or interests in land, and must not derive income from Vanuatu sources; beneficial ownership by Vanuatu tax residents is restricted. No industry license is required for the stated wooden-puzzle laser-assembly business; however, the company must contractually confirm that Amazon Pay and Stripe payment flows will be structured through a payment-facilitation or merchant-of-record arrangement, as neither provider currently lists Vanuatu as a direct supported country, and this structuring does not alter the VFSC incorporation deliverables.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - quantified at approximately 0.05 probability per annum for the registered office while the company remains fully compliant, with no PEP or sanctions hits, and with complete beneficial-ownership records maintained by the registered agent; inspection intensity is directed principally at the VFSC-licensed registered agent rather than the offshore e-commerce operations; the likelihood of unannounced physical inspection of a non-resident IC's overseas production facility is negligible, rising only upon FIU risk-flagging, unfavorable FATF/APG follow-up review outcomes, or a specific law-enforcement mandate.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 2013 (Cap 222), Vanuatu; ss. 4-10 (incorporation), s. 12 (registered office), s. 14 (registered agent), s. 28 (certificate of incorporation); read with the Companies and International Companies (Amendment) Act 2016
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) – International Companies Division and Companies Registry, Port Vila
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an International Company (FormIC-1) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Incorporation and Declaration of the Registered Agent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an International Company; shares may be issued at no par value and consideration may remain unpaid; no escrow account or capital deposit requirement is imposed
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Incorporation Application and Articles of Incorporation lodged with the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission are hereby ratified and adopted. RESOLVED, that the Company approves the allotment and issue of 100 ordinary shares of no par value to the subscriber for cash, credited as fully paid. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is fixed at the registered agent's office in Port Vila, Republic of Vanuatu. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as Director and [Name] is appointed as Company Secretary, each in accordance with the International Companies Act 2013. RESOLVED, that the Director and Company Secretary are authorised to open corporate bank accounts, execute business contracts, and engage professional advisers. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all acts taken in connection herewith are hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name reservation and restricted-word screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC Companies Registry – online i-Registry portal or physical counter at VFSC, Port Vila
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through a VFSC-licensed registered agent, certifying that the proposed name is not identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered name and contains no restricted words such as 'bank', 'trust', 'insurance', or 'assurance'. Obtain a written name availability approval notice before proceeding.
required_dossiers: Name availability certificate issued by VFSC
Consent of the proposed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit alternative names, remove restricted wording, or file an administrative appeal to the VFSC Registrar under s. 10 of the International Companies Act 2013 within 14 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution, notarization, and lodgement of incorporation instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC-licensed Registered Agent; Notary Public / Commissioner for Oaths of Vanuatu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Incorporation; the subscriber must execute the instruments before a notary public. The registered agent completes customer due diligence verification of identity and residence, then lodges the full application file with VFSC in hard copy or via i-Registry.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Incorporation (notarially executed)
Form IC-1 Application for Incorporation of an International Company
Consent to Act as Director (Form D-1)
Notarised certified copy of passport of each director, officer, and subscriber
Bank reference or certificate of identity for each beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VFSC issues a query notice, cure defects by filing a corrective statutory declaration and re-executed documents; minor irregularities are cured by supplemental filing without restarting the process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VFSC registration, payment of fees, and issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission – International Companies Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the executed incorporation file and pay the official fee of approximately USD 500 (VUV equivalent). VFSC examines the file, registers the company, and issues the Certificate of Incorporation and certified extracts of the register. The registered agent collects the certified documents for use in bank account opening and licensing.
required_dossiers: Registered agent and registered office consent letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected because of a document or name defect, re-file the corrected instruments within 30 days without additional penalty; an administrative appeal lies to the VFSC Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting, adoption of governance resolutions, and share issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; corporate secretary; registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting (actual or written resolution) at the registered office; adopt the First Board Resolution ratifying incorporation, approving share allotment, appointing the director and company secretary, and fixing the registered office. Issue share certificates, seal company registers, and prepare statutory minute book.
required_dossiers: Registered office consent and acceptance letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any procedural defect is cured by a subsequent board resolution ratifying and confirming the earlier actions; omitted statutory registers are prepared retroactively with a certificate of late filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal business licence application and post-incorporation regulatory notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Port Vila Municipality Business Licence Office (or Luganville Municipality, depending on operational premises); Department of Customs and Inland Revenue for statistical registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Municipal Business Licence under the Business Licence Act [CAP 220] covering 'Manufacture of Games and Toys – Wooden, Laser-Cut'. Submit the Certificate of Incorporation, premises plan, lease agreement, and identification of directors. Obtain premises inspection by the municipal building inspector; annual licence renewal thereafter. International Companies remain exempt from Vanuatu income tax, but may file a tax exemption certificate with the Department of Customs and Inland Revenue if required by counterparties.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation
Lease or ownership title of premises
Fire safety certificate issued by Vanuatu Police Force Fire and Rescue
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence application is refused, rectify premises deficiencies (fire extinguishers, ventilation, structural load) and re-submit within 14 days; an appeal lies to the Municipal Council and ultimately to the Minister of Finance and Economic Management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Industry, Ministry of Trade, Tourism, Industry and Cooperatives; Municipal Business Licence Authority of Port Vila / Luganville
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence – Category: Manufacturing of Wooden Games and Toys (ISIC 3240), subclass Laser-Cut Assembly Operations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC), Ministry of Climate Change, Vanuatu
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B2 – Environmental Registration (low-risk small-scale manufacturing); full EIA Report not triggered where installed footprint is under 500 m² and work shifts remain below 5 employees; registration certificate issued under s. 18 of the Environmental Management and Conservation Act 2005
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero hazardous liquid effluent to waterways or municipal drains; laser fume and VOC extraction to be filtered through HEPA/activated carbon systems with airborne wood dust controlled below 1 mg/m³ occupational exposure limit; solid wood waste segregated and recycled per Solid Waste Management Regulations 2019; noise level at boundary not to exceed 65 dB(A) during daytime operations

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Certificate from the Vanuatu Police Force Fire and Rescue Services confirming extinguisher placement, emergency egress, and flammable material storage; workplace registration with the Department of Labour under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2014; structural load and building occupancy inspection by the Port Vila Municipal Building Inspector; mandatory safety interlock and enclosure certification for the Class 4 CO2 laser cutting equipment

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Revenue Services (VRS), Ministry of Finance; online portal: https://vrs.gov.vu (VRS e-Services platform)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned International Company is incorporated under the International Companies Act through a licensed registered agent at the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC). No separate tax identification number or TIN is issued as a matter of course because the IC is non-resident and tax-exempt. If the IC elects to engage in domestic taxable activities or converts to an ordinary Vanuatu company, it must submit the Certificate of Incorporation, registered agent details, shareholder register, and a business activity declaration to the VRS; a VAT/TIN number is then issued within seven working days. For pure offshore export operations, the VFSC company registration number serves as the sole statutory tax identity reference.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections are available under Vanuatu law. The International Company is mandatorily exempt from domestic income tax, VAT, and stamp duties on all offshore operations and cannot elect a fictional passthrough or other hybrid status. The only statutory transformation route is an elective re-domiciliation or conversion to an ordinary company under the Companies Act, which would subject the entity to territorial ordinary company tax classification and VAT registration requirements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) administered by the Vanuatu Revenue Services under the Value Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory domestic VAT registration applies to any person with annual chargeable turnover exceeding VUV 5,000,000; however, a non-resident International Company whose only supplies consist of goods exported to non-Vanuatu customers has no VAT registration requirement because it lacks local economic nexus.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Vanuatu does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, government e-invoicing APIs, or digital stamping. Registered businesses issue self-generated VAT invoices in paper or electronic format containing the prescribed particulars; VAT returns and export substantiation documents are filed electronically via the VRS portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods is zero-rated under the VAT Act where the supplier exports the goods from Vanuatu within 28 days, or such longer period as the Commissioner allows, and retains sufficient proof of export. A supply of services is zero-rated where the recipient is a non-resident and the services are used wholly outside Vanuatu. An International Company engaged exclusively in export sales is not VAT-registered and therefore makes no VAT charge; if it were voluntarily registered, it would be entitled to zero-rated treatment on those export supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration duly stamped by the Vanuatu Customs Division
Original or electronic Bill of Lading / airway bill evidencing consignment to the overseas buyer
Commercial invoice and packing list reflecting the 0% VAT export status
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT statement evidencing receipt of payment from the non-resident purchaser
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims are subject to documentary audit by the Commissioner. Where the required export documentation bundle is incomplete or payment is not received within the 180-day repatriation deadline, the relevant supply is treated as standard-rated, attracting VAT plus late payment interest at 1.5% per month and an additional 25% penalty. Fraudulent zero-rating claims or falsified documents expose the taxpayer to criminal fines up to VUV 2,000,000 and imprisonment for up to five years; the Commissioner may also reassess VAT for up to six years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV), exercising statutory powers under the Exchange Control Act [Cap 65], the Banks Act [Cap 131], and the National Payments System Act No. 16 of 2021. The RBV administers all foreign exchange authorisations, licenses authorised dealers, and operates the national clearing and settlement infrastructure. The Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) is the parallel regulator for corporate service providers and the International Companies Act, while the RBV solely governs money and clearing policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vanuatu has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations and maintains unrestricted current-account convertibility for the Vatu (VUV). The regime distinguishes residents from non-residents: a VU International Company (IC) is statutorily treated as non-resident, allowing free holding of USD-denominated External Accounts, unrestricted crediting of export receipts, and remittance of dividends, interest, royalties, and liquidation proceeds without prior RBV consent. Capital-account flows are also liberal; share subscriptions and director loans into an IC require no exchange-control approval. Practical friction points are prudential, not statutory: (i) correspondent banks apply de-risking to VUV-linked flows; (ii) all inward transfers are screened against RBV/UN/EU sanctions lists; and (iii) any local-currency borrowing by an IC requires RBV approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory conversion ratio or quota exists in Vanuatu. Resident exporters must repatriate export proceeds within 180 days from date of shipment and may retain them in any convertible currency. A VU IC, being deemed non-resident, is exempt from the surrender obligation, the Form A approval requirement, and the local-currency conversion rule; its proceeds are credited directly to a designated USD External Account and may remain offshore indefinitely. The exporter must retain for five years the commercial invoice, bill of lading or airway bill, customs export declaration, and SWIFT credit confirmation to evidence the underlying trade on audit by the authorised dealer or RBV.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH as an ancillary collection and payout conduit, but LOW-MEDIUM as the primary liquidity depository. Offshore digital EMIs such as Airwallex, Currencycloud, Wise Business, and Mercury generally decline account opening for Vanuatu-incorporated International Companies due to historical FATF/EU listing and beneficial-ownership opacity; where approved, they offer only multi-currency wallets without VUV capability and impose strict USD transfer limits. Critically, Stripe and Amazon Pay do not settle natively into Vanuatu banks: a foreign settlement entity (Stripe UK Limited or a US/UK LLC merchant of record) is legally required to receive card rails, with onward SWIFT MT103 payouts to the Vanuatu External Account. Legal constraint: section 6 of the International Companies Act prohibits an IC from carrying on banking business in Vanuatu, but holding a normal corporate account with a licensed offshore EMI is permissible as long as funds originate from the IC's own trading and no deposit-taking is offered to third parties.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one signatory director is effectively mandatory for first-time IC account opening at all Vanuatu-licensed banks. The bank requires the director and each UBO holding 10% or more to attend an in-person interview at the bank's Port Vila branch with original passports; ANZ and BSP will exceptionally accept a video-conference interview only where the shareholder already has an existing banking relationship with the same banking group. Certified true copies of documents may be made by a notary or by a manager of another commercial bank, but the account signature card and the Foreign Exchange Declaration Form must be executed with wet ink before bank staff. Remote-only opening for a brand-new unlicensed IC is not available in the Vanuatu market.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bearer-share or unregistered beneficial ownership: VFSC company search shows nominee shareholders without a valid Beneficial Ownership (BO) declaration on file with the registered agent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the BO register lodged with the licensed registered agent; VFSC Certificate of Good Standing issued within 14 days; written BO declaration identifying each UBO above 10%; corporate organisational chart with shareholding percentages; passports and proof of residential address of all UBOs; copy of the registered agent's valid licence under the International Companies (Registered Agents and Registered Offices) Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Negative country risk / FATF or EU non-cooperative jurisdiction association attached to Vanuatu ICs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current RBV and VFSC compliance certificates; FATF statement confirmation of Vanuatu's removal from the grey list; documented economic substance for ISIC 3240 (leased Port Vila assembly premises, power and water utility bills, local employee records, equipment purchase invoices); CFO/accountant's letter confirming real trading; trade contract with Amazon or a merchant of record; 12-month transaction forecast in USD.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered-agent-only address with no physical operating presence; the IC appears as a shell with a single mailbox address.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly leased warehouse/office agreement in Port Vila or Luganville with six-month minimum term; interior and exterior photographs of the premises; utility bills in the IC's name; registered agent's certificate confirming the office arrangement and that the agent is licensed; business plan describing the CO2-laser cutting workflow and target markets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected activity mismatch: card-settlement inflows from Amazon Pay and Stripe are small and frequent, while outbound disbursements to laser-machinery suppliers in China/EU are large; the bank flags a laundering-via-trade pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trail of trade documentation: Amazon Seller Central statements; Stripe payout records; purchase orders; supplier proforma invoices matching unit economics (wood board, CO2 laser optics, electronics kits); export customs declarations; shipping waybills; inventory movement log; unit-cost markup calculation proving commercial rationality.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth opacity on the initial capital injection from a foreign shareholder resident in a high-risk or address-restricted jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Banker's reference letter from the remitting institution dated under three months; personal bank statements covering six months before the transfer; employment or dividend source documents; equity purchase agreement and board resolution authorising share subscription; statutory declaration of source of funds executed before a notary public.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Routing is via SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the shareholder's home bank to the IC's External Account at the Vanuatu authorised dealer. Compliance protocol: (a) the remitter name-field must exactly match the disclosed shareholder of record; (b) payment narrative must state SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION or DIRECTOR'S LOAN followed by the IC's legal name; (c) the bank files a copy of the board resolution approving the share allotment, the updated share register extract, and the VFSC annual confirmation; (d) no prior RBV exchange-control approval is required because the credit is to a non-resident External Account, but the bank must complete its internal Transaction Review; (e) funds whose narrative lacks a genuine business description are halted pending source-of-funds evidence; (f) after clearance, the Treasury maintains a USD liquidity buffer equal to at least 90 days of operating expenses in the External Account to absorb settlement delays from Stripe and Amazon Pay.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for supplier payments, logistics, freight, digital marketing, and software fees. For high-value capital purchases of laser tubes, MDF panels, and control electronics above VUV-equivalent USD 25,000, the Vanuatu bank issues irrevocable documentary Letters of Credit via SWIFT MT700, advised and confirmed by the beneficiary's bank, with 30-90 day tenors and charges of 0.25%-1.00% per annum plus opening fees. Recurring disbursements (Amazon FBA fees, Stripe charges, freight forwarders, SaaS subscriptions) are set up as standing instructions under a power of attorney, with each beneficiary screened against UN/EU/OFAC lists. Domestic VUV obligations, mainly staff wages and local utility charges, clear through the RBV National Payment System on a T+1 cycle. All outbound foreign payments above VUV 20,000,000 equivalent are formally recorded on the dealer's Exchange Control Form A, supported by the underlying contract and invoice, even for non-resident ICs, to preserve the bank's audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/VUV outright forwards with a licensed authorised dealer for up to 12 months, requiring production of the underlying trade invoice or purchase order at inception.
USD/VUV currency swaps with a licensed authorised dealer for medium-term matching of foreign-currency payables and receivables, subject to prior RBV approval on a case-by-case basis.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps on imported machinery loans where the exposure is demonstrably tied to the ISIC 3240 assembly capital expenditure programme, subject to RBV approval.

Natural hedging through multi-currency External Accounts: all trade revenue and operating costs retained in USD, with only minimum payroll and tax balances converted to VUV, thereby eliminating any material residual FX exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (confirmation of registered details) for International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), International Companies Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of each anniversary of incorporation; no fixed calendar date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty imposed by VFSC; continued failure to file or pay annual fee for more than six months triggers administrative strike-off of the International Company from the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government License Fee for International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) via Licensed Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable by the anniversary date of incorporation; renewal window begins 30 days before each anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Accrual of late penalties on unpaid fees; failure to pay by the end of the statutory grace period results in involuntary strike-off, loss of limited liability, and potential restoration fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Annual Confirmation of Compliance and Continuation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) through the appointed Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the Annual Return; no later than one month after the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-confirmation by the Registered Agent may lead to VFSC inquiry, suspension of corporate facilities, and eventual strike-off; agent has authority to resign under the International Companies Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: International Companies in Vanuatu are not subject to compulsory external audit. No statutory audit is required based on revenue, assets, capital, or annual turnover unless the company is separately licensed under a regulated activity (none applies to wooden puzzle laser assembly).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Companies Act does not prescribe IFRS or Local GAAP. Where financial records are prepared voluntarily for management or financing purposes, IFRS may be adopted, but statutory filing of financial statements is not required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Vanuatu International Companies maintain no public UBO register. The Registered Agent is required to identify the ultimate beneficial owner(s) on a risk-based KYC basis and must be notified within 14 days of any share transfer or beneficial ownership change. No separate annual UBO confirmation filing is required under the International Companies Act; however, the agent must always hold current UBO records and produce them to VFSC upon request.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable - no statutory audit requirement for this International Company

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory 0% corporate income tax on International Companies (ICs) under the International Companies Act [CAP 222]. Vanuatu imposes no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, and no branch profits tax on any entity. ICs are classified as tax-exempt offshore vehicles, so no statutory tax holiday, reduced-rate regime, or special deduction is needed; the permanent effective rate is 0%. The only indirect tax is Value Added Tax (VAT) at 12.5%, which applies to domestic supplies and imports; exported goods, such as laser-cut wooden puzzles sold via Amazon and Stripe to foreign customers, are zero-rated or fall outside the VAT net.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Vanuatu has no corporate income tax return. The sole statutory annual filing obligation for an International Company is the VFSC Annual Return (Form IC-AR), submitted electronically through the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) e-Services portal (www.vfsc.vu). No income tax return, no provisional tax return, and no capital statement is filed with the Vanuatu Department of Finance and Treasury, because the IC has zero income tax liability.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Return must be lodged within 6 weeks after each anniversary of the date of incorporation (Section 93, International Companies Act [CAP 222]). There is no tax-year-end filing deadline, since no income tax return exists; the anniversary-based deadline applies. The IC's financial year may be set freely, and no advance tax payment calendar applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The unique VFSC registration number assigned to the International Company at incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident filer must quote the certificate of incorporation number exactly as registered; no Vanuatu tax identification number is required because the entity is outside the income tax net.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Registered Office and Registered Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The physical address of the licensed registered agent in Vanuatu, which serves as the IC's statutory seat, service address, and records repository.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An IC must at all times maintain a registered office and a licensed agent in Vanuatu; the non-resident beneficial owner cannot substitute a foreign address, and the agent must hold the register of directors and shareholders at this location.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, residential or business addresses, and nationalities of every director and the corporate secretary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident individuals and corporate directors are expressly permitted; any nominee director arrangement must be disclosed to the registered agent, and the underlying beneficial owner must be identified in the AML/CFT file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and shareholdings of all members, including any transfers or changes in control during the preceding year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bearer shares are prohibited. Each beneficial shareholder must be recorded in the register kept at the registered office; non-resident shareholders may hold 100% of the IC, but must provide passport, proof of address, and source of funds for the VFSC-agent AML file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: A statutory declaration that the IC has complied with the International Companies Act, including record-keeping, registered-agent, and annual-filing obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The declaration must be signed by a director, secretary, or registered agent; a knowingly false declaration is a criminal offence and will trigger director disqualification and personal liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the VFSC Annual Return triggers a late-filing surcharge of approximately VUV 25,000 to 50,000 (USD 200 to 400) and an escalation of the annual government fee. Continued non-filing for more than one year results in the IC being struck off the register; all assets then vest in the government and the company name becomes unavailable for five years. Directors who fail to ensure filing face fines up to VUV 1,000,000, court-ordered restoration costs, and inability to act as directors of any registered Vanuatu entity.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Vanuatu imposes no withholding tax on dividends, and the International Company is taxed at 0% on all profits. Dividends, distributions, and capital reductions paid by an IC to any non-resident shareholder are paid gross with no Vanuatu deduction at source and no reporting to the Vanuatu tax authority.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Vanuatu maintains no comprehensive double taxation agreement (DTA) network, no dividend/interest/royalty treaty articles, and no treaty-rate relief mechanism. Consequently, there is no administrative process to invoke DTA relief, no tax-residency certificate (TRC) is issued to ICs, and no advance treaty-rate application exists. If the beneficial owner resides in a treaty-heavy jurisdiction, the exclusive route for relief is the recipient's domestic foreign-tax-credit regime, applied in the foreign jurisdiction; Vanuatu plays no role in that process. A written director's resolution authorizing each dividend, supported by audited or management accounts, is the only local formality.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on cross-border royalties and interest is 0% under Vanuatu domestic law, because no income tax withholding statute exists. The International Company may pay royalties to foreign IP owners and interest to foreign lenders entirely free of Vanuatu tax. No treaty rate is applicable because Vanuatu has no DTA network; therefore, the only tax exposure arises in the residence jurisdiction of the payee, and the IC should obtain a certificate of residence from its own legal counsel to support foreign tax credit claims abroad.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: N/A in Vanuatu vatu (VUV). Vanuatu has not enacted transfer pricing legislation and imposes no statutory Local File, Master File, or Country-by-Country Reporting (CbCR) threshold applicable to International Companies. No notional arm's-length profit margin filing exists. As a best-practice guard against foreign tax recharacterization, an IC with related-party transactions exceeding VUV 30,000,000 (approximately USD 250,000) annually should voluntarily maintain contemporaneous pricing documentation for the foreign parent's audit defense.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No domestic Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) equivalent to BVI or Cayman law are in force in Vanuatu. An International Company is only statutorily required to maintain a registered office and a licensed registered agent in Vanuatu; there is no legal requirement for local employees, local premises, local management, or active conduct of the wooden-puzzle assembly business in Vanuatu. However, under the OECD Inclusive Framework and EU Code of Conduct Group monitoring, an IC that is managed and controlled from a foreign jurisdiction may be deemed tax-resident there, and foreign courts may disregard the IC as a shell. Commercial substance should therefore be documented through real contracts, order-fulfillment records, pricing benchmarks, and board minutes even though Vanuatu itself does not demand them.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / VAT and Customs Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-invoicing exports of laser-manufactured wooden puzzles to reduce foreign import values; falsely zero-rating domestic Vanuatu sales; claiming VAT input credits on private or non-business expenses; and customs duty evasion on imported timber, laser machine parts, or finished goods through false tariff classification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Value Added Tax Act 2010 and the Customs Act 1998, civil penalties range from 50% to 100% of the evaded tax or duty, plus interest. Criminal conviction for fraudulent evasion carries fines up to VUV 10,000,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years, and any associated licences may be revoked by the VFSC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false VAT returns or customs declarations, or who direct third-party logistics providers to issue sham invoices, are personally liable for the evaded amounts through court-ordered civil restitution. Conviction additionally triggers disqualification from managing any Vanuatu company, and a court may impose a travel ban pending resolution of the tax fraud proceeding.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Commercial Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the International Company purely as a booking conduit: the wooden-puzzle business is fully managed and controlled by the non-resident owner from abroad, no bona fide trading records or board decisions exist, no warehouse or logistics oversight is maintained, and all material contracts are concluded by the foreign parent while Amazon and Stripe payment flows are routed through the IC solely to obtain the 0% Vanuatu rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vanuatu itself imposes no local penalty for such foreign control. However, a foreign tax authority may recharacterize the IC as resident in the owner's jurisdiction and assess undeclared profits at the full foreign corporate income tax rate, plus interest and penalties. The OECD Inclusive Framework peer-review process may also subject Vanuatu to reputational defensive measures that increase documentation scrutiny for all Vanuatu ICs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the non-resident owner/director intentionally uses the IC to defeat foreign tax claims, foreign courts can pierce the corporate veil and impose the entire foreign tax liability, interest, and penalties against the director personally. In habitual cases, the director faces a foreign court-issued travel ban and asset-freezing orders, and may be prohibited from acting as manager of any e-commerce vehicle.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving Amazon Pay and Stripe settlement funds through the IC without maintaining customer/KYC files, layering payments through multiple unrelated International Companies, converting funds into cryptocurrency or bearer instruments, or knowingly accepting proceeds from fraudulent online toy-store schemes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering under the Vanuatu Criminal Code, as amended by the AML/CFT regime, is punishable by imprisonment up to 20 years and/or fines up to VUV 50,000,000. The Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) and VFSC may freeze and confiscate the IC's assets, revoke the registered-agent licence, and report the matter to foreign partner FIUs for parallel prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners face personal criminal conviction, confiscation of personal assets, and disqualification from holding any VFSC licence or financial-officer role. The non-resident principal is subject to extradition and travel bans through Interpol red notices issued on Vanuatu's application, and any foreign shell intermediaries are similarly exposed to personal anti-money-laundering prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Filings / Fraud on the VFSC
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a false annual return, concealing a beneficial-ownership change, using fictitious or nominee directors without disclosure, presenting forged board minutes or shareholder consents to the registered agent, or failing to disclose an adverse foreign compliance event.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Contravention of the International Companies Act attracts fines up to VUV 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years. The VFSC may also strike the company off the register without further notice, refuse restoration where the filing was fraudulent, and permanently bar the entity and its officers from re-registering in Vanuatu.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The signing director and every director who authorized the false statement are jointly and severally liable for damages suffered by third parties. A civil court may lift the limited-liability veil and order personal restitution to defrauded creditors, and the offending director is prohibited from acting as a director or officer of any Vanuatu company for a mandatory period.
